llcFilesWith: Kentucky Secretary of State (Certificate of Assumed Name); one copy stamped filed by the Secretary of State must then be recorded with the county clerk of the county where the LLC maintains its registered agent for service of process, or its principal office if no registered agent is required. An entity that maintains neither in Kentucky files only with the Secretary of State
soleProprietorFilesWith: County clerk of the county where the individual maintains the principal place of business
feeBasis: KRS 365.015(11) sets the Secretary of State's fee at $20 for each certificate of assumed name, amendment, and renewal certificate; the county clerk receives a separate recording fee under KRS 64.012. Individuals pay only the county clerk fee.
renewalRule: An assumed name is effective for five years from the date of filing and is renewed for successive terms by filing a renewal certificate within the six months before the term expires, in the same offices as the original.
protectionNote: An assumed name discloses the name a business trades under and grants no exclusive right: KRS 365.015(7) provides that filing a certificate of assumed name does not automatically prevent the use of that name or protect it from use by other persons. Kentucky does screen entity assumed names on the way in, since KRS 365.015(2)(d) bars any certificate filed with the Secretary of State from setting forth an assumed name that is not distinguishable upon the Secretary of State's records from any other name previously filed and on record, so an active entity assumed name blocks a later filing that is not distinguishable from it.
searchNote: Assumed names filed by entities appear in the Secretary of State's business search, since they must be distinguishable upon those records. Assumed names filed by sole proprietors sit only in the relevant county clerk's records and are not in the state search.
notes: Kentucky splits its DBA system with an extra wrinkle. LLCs and other entities file a certificate of assumed name with the Secretary of State ($20), where KRS 365.015(2)(d) requires it to be distinguishable, and then record the filed copy with their county clerk, so an entity effectively files in two places. KRS 14A.3-050 routes every entity to KRS 365.015 for this. Individuals and sole proprietors file only with the county clerk where they do business. An entity files online from its own record in the Secretary of State's organization search, or on paper using form ASN. The assumed name is effective for five years and renewable, with no publication requirement at either level.
